ablations.note: Positive Brier/log-loss deltas mean the second model has lower error. They are predictive associations, not causal effects.

dataset.purpose: Cutoff-safe synthetic control pack for whether local-member stance improves held-out land-use prediction. This is a fixture control, not a recurrent population estimate.

kill_criterion.interpretation: Held-out stance lift after formal signals is above the recorded threshold and is not dominated by late evidence. That measurement still does not authorize a causal deference claim or production promotion.

negatives.error: outcome leakage in neg-leakage-outcome-before-cutoff: outcome_at must be after prediction_as_of
temporal leakage in neg-leakage-future-stance: feature follows cutoff
neg-invalid-cutoff.prediction_as_of must be an ISO timestamp

promotion.reason: Measured held-out lift does not authorize production promotion or a causal institutional-deference claim. The incumbent heuristic remains authoritative until a later gate.

protocol.existing_baseline_note: The production baseline emits cohort rates, not a project-level approval probability. This backtest reconstructs a comparable process-only logistic over application_type and procedural_stage so Brier and log loss can be compared without replacing the incumbent contract.

H1.claim: The local member's position independently predicts Council disposition because other members routinely defer to that member on local land-use matters.

H2.claim: The member's position predicts outcomes mainly because the member already observes negotiations, constituency response, applicant concessions, and project viability that CityScroll otherwise lacks.

rival_hypotheses.interpretation: Either mechanism may justify using stance as a predictive feature. This backtest does not distinguish H1 from H2 and does not assign a strong weight because institutional literature or domain theory predicts one.

split.rule: A case is train when prediction_as_of is on or before train_to, and test when prediction_as_of is on or after test_from. Labels use outcome_at strictly after the cutoff.
